title: The Silent Logs

beats.narrativeText: Power is restored to a small communications terminal, and fragments of the expedition logs become available.
Many sections of the recovered logs are corrupted, hinting that something unusual happened before communications stopped.
The learner reads the recovered logs carefully, gathering every available clue.
The learner arranges the events chronologically and highlights the most important evidence.
The learner must separate confirmed facts from reasonable assumptions within the damaged logs.
Piecing the fragments together, the learner discovers the name Dr. Elara Quinn for the first time.
The learner reflects on what the logs reveal — and what questions remain unanswered.
The expedition mystery officially begins, and the learner senses this is only the first piece of a much larger puzzle.

activities.title: Read Recovered Logs
activities.storyContext: Power has been restored to a small communications terminal, revealing fragments of the expedition's logs.
activities.instructions: Read through the recovered log fragments carefully.
activities.output: Notes on what each log fragment reveals.

activities.title: Arrange Events Chronologically
activities.storyContext: The logs are damaged and out of order, making the sequence of events unclear.
activities.instructions: Arrange the events described in the logs into the correct chronological order.

activities.title: Highlight Important Evidence
activities.storyContext: Not every detail in the logs is equally important.
activities.instructions: Highlight the pieces of evidence that seem most important to understanding what happened.
activities.output: A list of highlighted key evidence.

activities.title: Separate Facts From Assumptions
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy values evidence over assumption.
activities.instructions: Sort your findings into confirmed facts and reasonable assumptions.
activities.output: Two lists: confirmed facts and assumptions.

activities.title: Rewrite a Damaged Log Entry
activities.storyContext: Each expedition member would have experienced these events differently.
activities.instructions: Choose one damaged log entry and rewrite it from another expedition member's point of view.

activities.title: Reconstructing Incomplete Records
activities.storyContext: Reconstructing the expedition's logs is similar to how historians work with incomplete records.
activities.instructions: Find out how historians reconstruct incomplete historical records.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What is one fact you're certain of from the logs, and one thing you're only assuming?

discussionPoints: What clues helped you work out the correct order of events?
How can you tell the difference between a fact and an assumption?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a logically ordered sequence of events and a clear, justified separation between confirmed facts and assumptions.

completionCriteria: Recovered logs read, events arranged chronologically, and key evidence separated from assumptions.
